pr_body:
The `hashCode` implementation called `super.hashCode` which effectively (incorrectly) called `Object.hashCode`. The hash code didn't seem to be used anywhere, so removing made more sense than fixing.

The `equals` also looked a bit off as it did include `priority` from the parent class, but not `timeout`. Rather than implementing a proper equals method (in both `OperationModeUpdateTask` and `ClusterStateUpdateTask`, it's parent), I decided to just remove the method as I could only find one real use case, which was inside a test.

Closes #100871

issue_context.title: `OperationModeUpdateTask.hashCode` is incorrect
issue_context.body:
### Elasticsearch Version

8.10.3

### Installed Plugins

_No response_

### Java Version

Java 17

### OS Version

Windows 10

### Problem Description

The `hashCode` method of `org.elasticsearch.xpack.core.ilm.OperationModeUpdateTask` seems incorrect. It calls `super.hashCode`, but no superclass overrides the method, so effectively it calls `Object.hashCode` and therefore for two different objects their hash code will most likely always differ, even if they should be considered equal.

### Steps to Reproduce

```java
Object o1 = OperationModeUpdateTask.ilmMode(OperationMode.RUNNING);
Object o2 = OperationModeUpdateTask.ilmMode(OperationMode.RUNNING);

// This works
System.out.println("Equals: " + o1.equals(o2));
// This doesn't work; prints different hashCode values
System.out.println("hashCode:\n  o1: " + o1.hashCode() + "\n  o2: " + o2.hashCode());
```


### Logs (if relevant)

_No response_
